_meta.purpose: Single editable source of truth for the day orchestrator. Cadence, priority, and freshness are deliberately KNOBS — tuned by hand during the ~1-week parallel dry-run (Megan 2026-06-23).
_meta.scope: ALL non-upload reports run on the scheduler (Megan 2026-06-23). Frontier + Financial moved to auto email-ingest 2026-07-01. First/Last Sale RETIRED 2026-07-06.
_meta.weekday_convention: Python weekday(): Mon=0, Tue=1, Wed=2, Thu=3, Fri=4, Sat=5, Sun=6 (matches dashboard.py).
_meta.times: All times are CST (the mini is Central). HH:MM 24h.
_meta.priority_tiers: P1 critical (guaranteed done daily, runs first) > P2 standard > P3 best-effort (runs last).
_meta.freshness_target: A DEADLINE distinct from cadence. e.g. 'monday_am' = must be current by Monday morning even if deprioritized midweek; the orchestrator escalates effective priority as the deadline nears.
_meta.source_type: tableau = readiness gate + circle-back applies | appstream = immediately ready (no probe) | api = ready | upload = MANUAL, never auto-run.
_meta.run_order_flow: Run order optimizes TOTAL runtime (registry.flow_rank): wave 1 = every NON-tableau report (appstream / api / email / upload) so their early-ready data fills first; wave 2 = all source_type 'tableau' reports LAST, giving Tableau the most time to finish publishing before we read it; daily_rep_breakdown is pinned dead last (heaviest, flakiest). New reports auto-map by source_type — set it correctly and the report lands in the right wave automatically; no per-report order field. Source-type-based, never weekday-based, so a weekend-scheduled AppStream report still runs in wave 1 and is never blocked.
_meta.probe_not_configured: A tableau source with probe.type 'not_configured' resolves READY in --dry-run (so the full loop exercises) and NOT-READY in live (forces wiring the real view URL before cutover).
_meta.cutover_retire_jobs: These now run from the orchestrator — RETIRE their standalone LaunchAgents at cutover so reports don't double-run/double-post: com.alphalete.appstream-morning (daily_focus + Mon recruiter retention), com.alphalete.weather-6am, com.alphalete.brand-audit-noon, com.alphalete.recruiting-report (weekly ATT). Until cutover (dry-run week) they coexist safely — the orchestrator writes nothing.

close_stranded_incidents._off_scheduler_note: on_scheduler:false so it is NOT in the 4am batch. Present only so `lucy rerun close_stranded_incidents` can run `incident_thread --close-stranded` ON THE MINI. It finishes the incident parents whose white check landed but whose text still reads `open`: resolve() posts the reply, then edits the parent, and chat.update only touches your OWN messages -- so an incident opened by one machine and fixed from another keeps a parent that says `open` forever. Six were stranded on 2026-08-26 (four Lucy's, two Megan's laptop). It ONLY touches a parent that already carries the white check, so it can never close a real open problem, and it can only edit posts the machine it runs on wrote -- which is why it has to run on BOTH boxes: the laptop CLI for the laptop's, this entry for Lucy's.

install_mini_control_read_agent._off_scheduler_note: on_scheduler:false so it is NOT in the 4am batch. Present only so `lucy rerun install_mini_control_read_agent --machine "<name>"` can install com.alphalete.mini-control-read -- the READ LANE of the Mini Control queue. The queue is ONE serial worker, so a 2-second `logtail` waits behind whatever report is in front of it: on 2026-08-27 a 3-chunk ad_sales_board backfill (~22 min each) held it from 09:36 and fourteen rows stacked up behind, including a tableau_screenshots `text_tracker` that went out an hour late, while every diagnostic read as a dead poller. The read lane is the same module with lane 'read' and takes ONLY the READONLY_ACTIONS (logtail, daystate, git_status, git_diff, slack_channel, slack_find, slack_thread). SAFE beside a live report: nothing in that set writes a Sheet, sends a message, or touches the shared browser profile. The lanes split the queue by action name so they can never claim the same row, and each reclaims only its own orphans -- the read lane will NOT mark main's 22-minute rerun orphaned. Installing this changes NO report behaviour; the worst a bad fire does is leave the reads where they are today, behind main. Goes through install_agent, which only loads the plist -- read-only w.r.t. any Sheet data.

install_incident_triage_agent._off_scheduler_note: on_scheduler:false so it is NOT in the 4am batch. Present only so `lucy rerun install_incident_triage_agent` can install the com.alphalete.incident-triage LaunchAgent (8:15am and then every 2h to 16:15, deploy/incident_triage.sh) on the mini. That pass SORTS the open incidents in #claudecorrections-and-requests and reacts: red circle = needs Megan or Eve personally, :pending: = Lucy is still retrying it, purple = waiting on a source. It NEVER re-runs a report and NEVER edits code, so the worst a bad fire can do is put one wrong emoji on a post. Mini only: Slack lets you remove your OWN reaction and nobody else's, so a circle added under a person's token could never be taken off again (same rule as incident_working). 8:15 is after the flow's main passes and the 7:30 checkpoint email, and well before the noon backstop -- triaging mid-flow would grade reports the orchestrator is still actively retrying. It REPEATS every 2h to 16:15 (Megan 2026-08-27): a single 8:15 pass made classify()'s noon backstop rule unreachable (nothing ever ran with now_hour >= 12) and left an incident opened after 8:15 -- or a mark that failed to land -- with no answer on it until the next morning. Re-running is quiet: the reaction is idempotent and the thread line goes in once per STATE CHANGE, not once per pass.

install_session_holder_agent._note: MANUAL-ONLY (weekdays []). `lucy rerun install_session_holder_agent --machine "<machine>"` installs com.alphalete.session-holder, which keeps the ownerville login warm and EXPORTS .ownerville_storage_state.json every 6 min. WHY THIS ENTRY EXISTS (Megan 2026-08-23): every other LaunchAgent had an install_* entry but the holder did not, so a new machine could be fully provisioned and still never run a single scheduled report. readiness.session_status() is a MACHINE-GLOBAL gate — the exported file must exist AND be <20 min old (settings.session_stale_after_minutes) — so a machine with no holder fails EVERY report at every pass with 'still trying — no ownerville session yet'. That is exactly what happened on Lucy 3's debut morning 2026-08-23: day-orchestrator fired on time (morning_diag DRIFT=+0m) and then held all 5 of its reports for 4+ hours; the Country Trackers reached no channel until a manual rerun. Do NOT be fooled by a manual `lucy rerun` succeeding on an unseeded machine — _ensure_ownerville_logged_in falls back to the persistent PROFILE cookie, but the readiness gate only ever checks the holder's FILE. AFTER INSTALLING, A HUMAN MUST SEED IT ONCE at that machine's screen: the holder opens ownerville and waits up to 15 min for a human to log in and clear Cloudflare's Turnstile (there is no unattended path past a forced interactive challenge). Until seeded, the plist's KeepAlive + ThrottleInterval 30 just relaunches it every 30s. Confirmed 2026-08-23 that two machines CAN hold Raf's ownerville concurrently (Megan), so Lucy 3 does not need its own account. on_scheduler:true ONLY so registry keeps it; weekdays [] = never auto-runs. source_type 'local'. Safe/idempotent.

all_campaigns_board._note: Fills the 'All Campaigns Org Sales Board' tab's per-person 'All Units' daily section. It's a campaign-AGNOSTIC product-totals ranking: unlike the ORG Sales Board it does NOT split a rep by campaign — one line per person = SUM across every campaign. Reads the already-filled 'Alphalete ORG Sales Board' tab's eight daily sections (Retail NL, ATT Fiber Team, Retail JE, ATT NDS Team, B2B, BOX, Frontier, Retail Internet), sums each rep by normalized name across all of them, and writes the Mon-Sun day cells via the ORG board's fill_section engine. Everything else on the tab is formula-driven (running total =SUM, leaderboard =SUMIF, Product Summary/vs-Prior) and auto-derives. `after` org_sales_board (SOFT: runs once the board reaches ANY terminal state, so a board INCOMPLETE — which is common — never strands this) rather than depends_on. base_args '--apply' = LIVE write. Validated + ROLLED OUT LIVE 2026-07-24 (Megan): aggregated grand-total-per-day matched the Copy tab's Grand Total row exactly; 38/38 board rows matched, 0 unmatched. Auto-fires daily (weekdays [0..6]) right after the board. TUESDAY ROLLOVER (base_args '--enable-rollover', validated + approved by Megan 2026-07-24): same fixed-window system as the Copy tab — self-heals off the leaderboard week header, so it rolls on the first run of the new reporting week (Tuesday) and is a no-op otherwise. NO columns/rows grow: the weekly leaderboard shifts C(this wk value)->D->..->G with the oldest week DROPPED; the daily per-rep running total shifts J->K->L (L lost); the WE-history rows shift down (oldest dropped); the delta box freezes this-week->last-week; then day cells clear + the date anchor advances. Snapshots to backup_pre_rollover_allcampaigns first. `lucy rerun all_campaigns_board` runs it on demand. Exits 75 (INCOMPLETE) if a board rep never matched the pull, or a producing rep has no board row (flagged, never silently dropped).
all_campaigns_board._data_sources_note: GATED ON THE BOARD ITSELF, not just on the board's exit code (Eve 2026-09-01). `after: org_sales_board` is soft ordering and treats INCOMPLETE as terminal, so on a morning where the board exits 'partial' BEFORE it has actually written yesterday's column this fill runs ~30 min later against an empty source, writes a whole day of ZEROS, exits 0 (a 0 is non-blank, so `verify` passes too), is recorded DONE and never runs again. It happened on Tue 2026-09-01: org_sales_board partial 04:27, this ran 05:01, and because Tuesday ALSO rolls the week, the tab spent the morning showing 0 for every rep on the new week while the board's later passes (07:18 / 08:36 / 09:39) filled the ORG tab and nothing re-filled this one. sheet:org_board_yesterday -> readiness._probe_org_board_filled -> org_sales_board.data_gate.gate(): ready once YESTERDAY's column on 'Alphalete ORG Sales Board' is filled for every section but the day-behind ones (data_gate.LAGGING_SECTIONS), and it FAILS OPEN past data_gate.SEND_ANYWAY_AFTER, so a board that never fills cannot also cost the day's fill. Gating in READINESS keeps a late board STILL_TRYING — re-probed every pass, no burnt retries, no red pill — instead of one early DONE nobody can see. Same gate the org board email used before it moved to slack:org_board_posted.

country_sales_board_email._duplicate_guard_note: OPTED OUT OF THE DUPLICATE-RUN GUARD (Eve 2026-09-01). The guard identifies a running report by MODULE NAME alone: proc_guard.running_pids builds its pgrep pattern from command[0] and anchors it right after the module, so every argument is invisible to it. This report's module, board_emails.review_gate, is ALSO what deploy/org_board_email_review.sh runs every 15 minutes from 07:00 to 20:00 to poll for the approval checkmark - a completely different job on the same box. The two are indistinguishable to the guard, so the daily --post can lose a race to a --check tick, and on 2026-09-01 it did: the pre-launch guard cleared at 08:54:53, a checker tick started, and the LAST-LINE-OF-DEFENCE guard inside run._run_report failed the report at 08:54:56. Three seconds. That second path returns a hard FAILURE rather than the pre-launch deferral, so it burned the attempt, fired the incident and wrote no log at all (the alert said 'no log captured' because the log file is created just before the subprocess that never launched), and the review link never went up - on a board that had filled perfectly. The guard exists for browser reports fighting over the shared Chrome profile, and review_gate opens no browser: it reads the Sheet over OAuth and exports PDFs, so the collision it protects against cannot happen here. Two --post runs at once are harmless besides - review_gate deletes the day's older posts before it posts. The Org board's twin never hit this because its --post runs from its own LaunchAgent (com.alphalete.org-board-review-post.plist), not from this batch, so it bypasses the guard entirely. This is the ONLY report with the flag off, and test_duplicate_run_guard.SharedModuleOptOut pins that.

country_sales_board._note: Fills the 'Country Sales Board' tab's per-ICD daily block ('Fiber - All Units') and runs its TUESDAY rollover. Modelled on all_campaigns_board and slotted right after it, i.e. after the 'Alphalete ORG Sales Board' block (Eve 2026-07-27). SOURCE IS TABLEAU, NOT THE COPY TAB — unlike all_campaigns_board this one does its own crosstab download: ATT Tracker 2.1 - D2D / D2D 1-PAGERV4, worksheet 'Sales By ICD (ATT) (V2)', which is the 'D2D Page 1 - This Week' tracker (its header row literally reads 'This Week'). One crosstab in, seven day columns out; the leaderboard =SUMIF, Totals =SUM, Product Summary and Current-vs-Prior all derive themselves, so the fill writes ONLY the Mon-Sun day cells. The view's two windows are relative and NOT filterable by week, so pull.pull_icd_days_aligned checks which week came back and falls back to the '(LW2)' worksheet if 'This Week' doesn't cover the board — a source that ever rolls a day early can never smear one week into another week's columns. TUESDAY ROLLOVER (base_args '--enable-rollover'): keyed off week.reporting_sunday, so it fires on the first run of the new reporting week and is a no-op every other day; a missed Tuesday rolls Wednesday. MONDAY never rolls (Monday's fill writes SUNDAY into the closing week). Snapshots to 'Country Sales Board (pre-rollover backup)' before touching anything. VALIDATED 2026-07-27 (Eve): fill engine reproduced the VAs' own frozen WE 07.19 leaderboard column 75/75 EXACT off the 7/20 crosstab, 0 differences — the only delta was Blue Mendoza, blank on the VA column because her row postdates that freeze and correctly 50 from the automation. Rollover run live end-to-end on the sandbox (WE 07.26 -> WE 08.02): leaderboard grows right, WE stack insert + Current-vs-Prior re-anchor, per-rep J->K->L, day cells clear, and it is a no-op on every later day of the week. POST-WRITE VERIFICATION (Eve 2026-07-27): the run re-reads the sheet and asserts the day block's Totals row carries NUMBERS for YESTERDAY — the day it reports on, and always the newest column with data. A zero or blank there exits 1, so the orchestrator marks it FAILED and the failure alert fires. This exists because there is no `verify` manifest for this report, so a run that completed having written nothing used to exit 0 and be recorded DONE with nobody told. It reads the TOTALS row (a =SUM over the cells just written), which proves both that the numbers arrived AND that they landed inside the ranges the board's own aggregates cover. Every early-return path is gated by it too, including the 'no data yet' one. A country-wide 0 is a real signal: this board does ~7,000 units a week and its quietest day still runs ~190. Escape hatch: --no-verify. Unmatched board ICDs, by contrast, are WARNED, never a non-zero exit — 5 rows (Edgar Muniz II, Niko Figueroa, Mason Davis, Mary Maya, Jacob Morgan) are inactive reps absent from the view sitting at a correct 0.
country_sales_board._warn: LIVE ON THE REAL TAB since 2026-07-27 (Eve, after the sandbox validation in _note) — base_args carries '--real --i-mean-it', so this writes 'Country Sales Board', the tab the country reads and the one the VAs used to key BY HAND. THE VAs MUST NOT ALSO ROLL IT: two rollovers on one tab in one Tuesday double-shift the leaderboard (every frozen week lands one column too far right) and push a second WE row into the history stack. The Tuesday roll snapshots to 'Country Sales Board (pre-rollover backup)' before touching anything — that is the tab to restore from if it ever happens. To back out, drop '--real --i-mean-it' from base_args and it returns to 'Country Sales Board (sandbox)'; nothing else changes.

country_sales_board_slack._note: Screenshots the 'Country Sales Board' tab (exact-sheet PDF-export render, no browser — same path as org_board_slack / all_campaigns_board_slack) and sends it as ONE shared Slack GROUP DM (all recipients in a single mpim thread, needs the bot's mpim:write scope) under a DATED title — 'Country Sales Board 7.26' on a 7/27 run. The date is YESTERDAY, not the run date (Eve 2026-07-27): the fill only writes COMPLETED days, so the last day carrying numbers is always the day before, and titling it with the run date would date the message a day ahead of the sales it shows. Anchored to America/Chicago, and correct across month/year boundaries (a 8/1 run titles 7.31). RECIPIENTS ARE THREE, deliberately fewer than the All Campaigns DM's five (Eve 2026-07-27): Rafael Hidalgo, Maud Miller, Evelyn Sobrino — no Carlos, no Megan. Hard-coded Slack user IDs in slack_post.RECIPIENTS (no users:read dependency). NOT A WHOLE-TAB SHOT, AND NOT ONE RANGE: this tab runs to row 310 x column BC (52 frozen leaderboard weeks), so a full render is an unreadable postage stamp and a single contiguous range spanning both blocks would drag in ~135 rows of day block and WE history between them. It renders TWO blocks and stitches them into one image: (1) the BOARD — row 1 through the leaderboard TOTALS row, cols A..J = title + Product Summary + Current vs Prior through Grand Total + the full rep ranking with 7 weeks of trend; (2) the DELTA UNITS CHART — cols B..Z, the per-rep 'Total for week' triplet plus ALL SEVEN DAYS as This week / Last week / Delta, down to and including the country-wide TOTALS row. Eve asked for the delta chart with every day after seeing the first version without it (2026-07-27). Both blocks are located BY LABEL each run (leaderboard header + org_sales_board.find_delta_tables), so an inserted row or a new rep can't silently crop the image; find_delta_tables stops at the first nameless row, which is the TOTALS row itself, so slack_post pulls that one back in deliberately. Sends AS LUCY via the provisioned 'Lucy Reporting' USER token (slack-user-token) — NOT a bot app; SLACK_BOT_TOKEN was never created on the mini, so `--as-bot` is only for a runner where one has been seeded (Lucy 2). Run it from a machine whose slack-user-token is NOT Lucy's (e.g. Eve's laptop) and it sends from that account instead. `--post` = LIVE send; without it the run is a dry-run that still builds the PNG. Proving send to one person: `--only U088E2KJEV8 --post`. On-demand: `lucy rerun country_sales_board_slack` (uses base_args, so it sends).

knocks_access_watch._note: READ-ONLY WATCHER, NOT A REPORT (Eve 2026-08-25). Reads the ownerville Office Access list of the reporting account (rhidalgo) and the captainship rosters off the Org Sales Board, and says which ICDs the knock boards can reach. Posts to #claudecorrections-and-requests ONLY when that set CHANGES - an office granted (it is now in its captain's boards) or lost. Silent otherwise, on purpose: a watcher that announces 'still 19 of 35' every pass teaches everyone to skip it. WHY IT EXISTS: 16 of the 35 fiber-captainship ICDs had no Office Access on 2026-08-24, the reports shipped partial from 8/25 (grey 'no access' note per missing owner, '(N of M ICDs)' on the totals row), and the grants arrive one at a time from someone else's console with no notification. Nothing in the code needs updating when one lands - the boards are built from the Sales Board roster, so the office simply starts pulling - this is only how we FIND OUT. It takes the ownerville session (one per account), so it waits for the knock pulls to finish and skips the pass rather than interrupting one; exit is always 0, a skipped pass is not a failure. The intraday goteo runs off com.alphalete.knocks-access-watch (10:30/13:30/16:30/19:30) - see install_knocks_access_watch_agent. Retire both when every ICD is granted.

captainship_knocks._machine_note: MOVED TO LUCY 3 2026-08-25 (Megan, approved 8/24). This ~2h ownerville capture dominated Lucy 1's morning; Lucy 3 is idle 04:22-06:42 (tableau_screenshots ends 04:22, tableau_screenshots_box does not start until 06:42), so the capture now runs in a window that was empty and Lucy 1's queue gets its two hours back. SAFE TO RUN CONCURRENTLY WITH LUCY 1's OWNERVILLE WORK: impersonation is scoped to the ColdFusion SESSION, not the account - _exit_impersonation returns 'the server's session' to master mode and _find_owner_and_impersonate gets a fresh per-session rqst - and each Lucy logs into ownerville itself (mini_control._CRED_FILES pushes ownerville-creds.json, never the storage_state cookies). Two machines can therefore impersonate on the same account at once. NOTE THE TENSION, it is deliberate: daily_rep_breakdown._machine_note (2026-08-22) fences ITSELF at 05:00 to stay clear of 'Lucy 1's 4:00-4:45 ownerville window (SAME rhidalgo account; concurrent logins can kick sessions)'. That fence predates Megan's 2026-08-24 correction and is the cautious read of the same facts. This entry follows the correction. If knock captures start coming back short or Lucy 1's early ownerville reports start failing on kicked sessions, THAT is the symptom - put a cadence.not_before '05:15' on this entry (after Lucy 1's board fill ends ~05:14) and the two never overlap again.

captainship_knocks._note: THE EXPENSIVE HALF OF captainship_drafts, SPLIT OUT (Eve 2026-08-24). One ownerville session impersonates every ICD of the six fiber captainships in single file - ~2h measured 8/24 - and that LOOP cannot be parallelised WITHIN a session, because each impersonation replaces the last. Corrected 2026-08-24 (Megan): this is NOT an account-wide limit. Impersonation is scoped to the ColdFusion SESSION - _exit_impersonation returns 'the server's session' to master mode, and _find_owner_and_impersonate gets a fresh per-session rqst - and each Lucy logs into ownerville itself (mini_control._CRED_FILES pushes ownerville-creds.json, never the storage_state cookies). So two machines CAN impersonate on Raf's account at the same time, which is what makes moving this capture to Lucy 3 safe. CAPTURES ONLY: no Sheet write, no mail, no Slack. captainship_drafts then finds these images through knock_dispo_images' per-captain manifest and opens no session at all, which is what turns a rebuild - or the 07:15 review-link agent building the previews itself - back into a minutes-long job instead of a two-hour one that also blocks every other job on the mini. If this step fails nothing breaks: the build pulls whatever the manifest doesn't cover, exactly as it did before the split.

captainship_knocks._after_note: `after: org_sales_board` DROPPED 2026-08-25 with the move to Lucy 3 - it had become an ordering nobody could enforce, exactly like daily_rep_breakdown's on the same day. org_sales_board runs on Lucy 1 and day state is per machine (output/day_state/<date>.json is local), so Lucy 3 can never see its status; deps.py classifies that as KIND_OTHER_MACHINE, and a SOFT `after` in that bucket runs anyway while alerting through _alert_unenforceable_deps on EVERY pass. Keeping it would have bought no ordering and one guaranteed #claudecorrections alert every morning. WHAT IS ACTUALLY LOST: the capture reads the Org Sales Board roster, and at ~04:22 on Lucy 3 that read now lands BEFORE Lucy 1's board fill (04:56-05:14) instead of after - so a captaincy roster change made yesterday reaches the knock boards one day late. Judged acceptable because reading the previous roster was already the tolerated fallback (the old note: on a morning the board fill FAILS the capture still runs on the previous roster) and the roster changes rarely. If that one-day lag ever matters, the fix is cadence.not_before '05:15' on this entry, NOT putting the `after` back.

Duplicates the Sales Board tab, clears the VA's basic filter on the COPY, then per program hides non-campaign + terminated rows and renders (a) the weekly ranking and (b) the Highrollers cut for yesterday, posting them as one dated thread 'Vantura Production MM/DD/YYYY' AS LUCY to TWO channels: #alphalete-gp-sales (C07J46MQNUX, boards only) and #a-players-b2b (C0AJQA8P716, boards PLUS the Zero Streak replies — Carlos 2026-07-23). TIMEOUT 35, deliberately above RECOVER_WAIT_MIN (20): with both at 20 the wrapper killed the run at the exact moment its wait ended, so it could never report success — it looked like a failed heal when the heal had simply not been allowed to finish (2026-08-31).
